# Selection models share their selection arrays per class: selectedRows / selectedColumns (grid) and selectedRowIds / selectedColumnCellIds (table) are static-config defaults, so two grids on one model class select together

## Context

Two grids on the same selection-model class share one selection today. Measured 2026-09-13 in the engine's unit runtime (Playwright `unit` project, dev-equivalent source at `agent/18626-view-owned-selection@8d8799643e`, `src/selection/grid/BaseModel.mjs` unchanged from dev): `Neo.create(RowModel).selectedRows === Neo.create(RowModel).selectedRows` is `true`; after `modelA.selectedRows.push(3)` a fresh `Neo.create(RowModel).selectedRows` reads `[3]`; `RowModel.config.selectedRows` is that same array. CellRowModel, CellModel and ColumnModel each share their own copy per class; the table family declares the same kind of static arrays under its own names. CI surfaced it first: unit job 103741193182 (PR #18661, head `8d8799643e`) ran two grid arms in one worker in file order — a RowModel grid selected record 3 and was destroyed, the next RowModel grid adopted records 2 and 4 from its own store and read `[3, 2, 4]`; the retry ran alone and passed. In an app: a Workstation with two grids on the default `RowModel` and colliding business ids paints a row in the second grid the moment the first selects it, and the second grid's `singleSelect` deselects the first's row.

## The Problem

`src/selection/grid/BaseModel.mjs:21` and `:27` declare `selectedColumns: []` and `selectedRows: []` as NON-reactive static configs. `core.Base#mergeConfig` (`src/core/Base.mjs:764`, `{...staticConfig, ...config}`) copies a static default by reference and `setFields` assigns it as the instance's own property — so a mutable default is one object per class, and `NeoArray.add(me.selectedRows, recordId)` / `NeoArray.remove` (`BaseModel.mjs:238, 363`) mutate the class's array in place. `BaseModel#unregister` (`:394`) assigns the DESTROYED instance a fresh `[]` and leaves the class array populated for the next instance. The table family repeats the pattern: `selectedRowIds: []` (`src/selection/table/CellRowModel.mjs:29`) and `selectedColumnCellIds: []` (`src/selection/table/CellColumnModel.mjs:34`, `src/selection/table/CellColumnRowModel.mjs:34`) — five static arrays across the selection family. `Neo.selection.Model#items_` (`src/selection/Model.mjs`) already carries the per-instance descriptor; the subclasses' arrays never got it.

## The Architectural Reality

This is the #18198 class — `grid.Body`'s row and column windows were the same static-array default, fixed with config descriptors after the maintainer's ruling there (descriptors are the Neo-native shape; a `construct()` copy and instance fields were dropped). The config-system side (why a static reference default is not cloned per instance) is D#18195 / #18192 and stays there.

## The Fix

The five arrays — grid `selectedColumns_` / `selectedRows_`, table `selectedRowIds_` / `selectedColumnCellIds_` (twice) — become reactive configs with the `Neo.selection.Model#items_` / `grid.Body#mountedRows_` descriptor: `{[isDescriptor]: true, clone: 'shallow', cloneOnGet: 'none', value: []}` — `clone` makes the default per instance, `cloneOnGet: 'none'` keeps the in-place `NeoArray.add` / `remove` writes landing (the engine's default copies arrays on every read, so a write would land in a discarded copy). Every reader and writer keeps its name (`me.selectedRows`, `me.selectedColumns = [...]`, `me.selectedRowIds`, `toJSON`). The full invariant closes in one commit — a partial fix of a shared-state invariant burns the next review cycle (#14153).

## Contract Ledger

Not applicable: no public surface changes shape — all five members keep their names, types and semantics; only their per-instance identity is repaired.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 Two grids on the same model class hold distinct `selectedRows` and `selectedColumns` arrays; a row selected in the first is not held or painted by the second.
- [ ] AC-2 A grid created after another grid on the same model class was destroyed starts with an empty selection.
- [ ] AC-3 Every grid and table selection model instance owns its arrays: an identity arm over the nine model classes (`selectedRows`, `selectedColumns`, `selectedRowIds`, `selectedColumnCellIds` distinct per instance, an in-place push on one instance invisible to a fresh one) — red on the current source.
- [ ] AC-4 The existing selection arms (`unit/grid`, `unit/selection`, e2e `SelectionMultiBody`, `BigDataMultiBodyNL`) stay green; `unit/grid/ViewOwnedSelectionModel.spec.mjs` is deterministic in any worker order (AC-1 / AC-2 are red on the current source too).

## Out of Scope

The config-system gap (D#18195 / #18192); `Neo.selection.Model#items_` (already a descriptor); the `add: []` literals in `GalleryModel` / `HelixModel` (method-local update payloads, not defaults).

## Avoided Traps

- Instance fields (`selectedRows = []`) or a `construct()` copy — dropped in #18198 by the maintainer; descriptors are the shape.
- A descriptor without `cloneOnGet: 'none'` — the default read copy would swallow every in-place write (#18198's second finding).
- Reading the leak as a test-ordering flake and re-keying the spec's records per arm — that hides the defect the arm just measured.
